name: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
summary: Look up relevant documents first, then give them to the model to answer from.

D1.guide: When you're unsure of an answer, what do you do before replying?
text: If you ask a friend a question about your school, they might check the school website before answering.
RAG makes the AI look things up first instead of guessing from memory.
Documents are split into chunks and turned into vectors (**embeddings**) stored in an index.
At question time the question is embedded too; the closest chunks are retrieved, often combined with keyword search and re-ranked, and placed in the prompt.
The model answers from that context, ideally with citations. Quality depends mostly on retrieval: if the right chunk isn't found, the model can't use it.
D2.analogyBreaks: In an open-book exam you choose what to read. In RAG the model only sees what retrieval hands it, and it can still blend in its own, possibly wrong, memory.

predict.question: A RAG assistant gives a wrong answer even though the correct document is in the index. What should you check first?
options: Whether retrieval actually returned the right chunk
predict.explanation: Most RAG failures are retrieval failures: poor chunking, embeddings or ranking mean the right text never reached the model.

text: Open problems: agentic retrieval where the model decides what to search, long-context models versus retrieval, measuring faithfulness to sources, and poisoning of indexed content.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
